ca_central_boulder.blurb: A single large boulder in the middle of Boulder Gulch Campground, in the Kern Valley of the southern Sierra, with essentially no walk from the car. It has eight problems, from V0 up to V4: three at V1, a pair at V3 and a pair at V4, so the grades lean toward the middle with a couple of harder lines on top. Several of the problems are on the north face, which loses the sun by late in the day. It suits a short session with a pad, and the other boulders in the gulch add more problems nearby.

ca_box_canyon_area.blurb: A small sub-area of the Comic Book Area in central Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,400 feet. It has eight routes, nearly all of them trad with a single bolted line. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.12a: two at 5.8, one at 5.9, four around 5.10 and two at 5.12. The routes include a flat wall, a thin hands crack and other crack and face lines, so bring a standard rack. Expect a trail walk from the road that can take anywhere from a few minutes to half an hour or more depending on which formation you are heading to.

ca_breeze_way.blurb: Breeze Way is a small section of the Third Tier on El Cajon Mountain in San Diego County, on a long sloping, grassy ledge high above the lower tiers. It has eight routes split evenly between trad and sport, one to three pitches long, from 5.8 up to 5.12a, with three around 5.10 and a pair at 5.11. Getting there is part of the day: the ledge is reached by walking up through the lower tiers, with some bushwhacking, a faint trail and a short handline before the base.

ca_bridge_boulder.blurb: A granite boulder about ten feet tall, tucked into the trees beside a stream in the Arroyo Seco canyon of the Angeles National Forest above Altadena. It has eight problems from V1 to V3, with five of them at V2. Holds are mostly solid and grippy, though some are smooth and polished, and one jug is a little loose. The boulder sees few visitors, so it tends to be dirty and webbed, and a brush is worth carrying. The way in is a walk of roughly a mile and a half along a road that turns to dirt, past a second bridge.

ca_bukit_timah_usa.blurb: A cluster of eight boulders in the pines of the Pine Mountain Club and Mount Pinos region of southwestern Kern County, at roughly 8,000 feet. Most of the problems are V0, with one easier line and a single V3, and a few of the taller rocks lend themselves to scrambling or harder projects. The ground is covered in pine needles and fallen timber, and getting here means an off-trail walk of a couple of miles beyond the Mount Pinos campground area. Nordic Base Boulder sits about two miles uphill if you want to add a second stop.

ca_buttocks_boulder.blurb: One boulder among the Dreamers group on the Sherwin Plateau above Mammoth Lakes, at about 7,000 feet in the Eastern Sierra. It sits just past the entrance boulders, to the left. The main feature is a slabby west-facing wall, with a short, narrow vertical face at the left end. There are eight problems and all are on the easy side: four are VB, one is V0, one V1 and two V2. The rock is pocketed tuff. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons here, since summer heat builds even at this altitude.

ca_castle_rock_south_side.blurb: One side of Castle Rock, the oblong formation at the center of Belle Campground in the Pinto Basin of Joshua Tree National Park, at about 3,800 feet. The climbing here is slab-oriented, on coarse, gritty stone, and every route is trad. Eight routes run from 5.6 to 5.12, with five of them at 5.9 and one each at 5.6, 5.7 and 5.12. There is no real approach: you walk through the campground to the base.

ca_cereal_rock.blurb: A roadside formation in Joshua Tree National Park, close to Hidden Valley and the Steve Canyon area, with routes on several sides of the rock. There are eight routes here, almost all trad plus a single bolted line, running from about 5.6 to 5.10. Six of them sit around 5.10, so the grades cluster toward the harder end of the range with a couple of easier options. The walk from the road is short, on trails.
ca_cereal_rock.parking_note: Use one of the paved pullouts along Park Boulevard near Intersection Rock; the formation is visible from the first pullout west of that rock.
ca_cereal_rock.approach: A trail walk of five to ten minutes from the roadside pullout to the formation.
